status: locally reviewed; no push or deployment

sourceVintage.morth: Road Accidents in India 2024, calendar-year police returns, with direct 2023 comparisons
sourceVintage.supremeCourt: Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan, 2026 INSC 647, judgment of 19 June 2026
sourceVintage.who: Pedestrian safety: a road safety manual for decision-makers and practitioners, 2023; general prevention guidance

sections.heading: How many pedestrians are killed on India's roads?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Table 4.4, PDF p98; victim-category rows and national 2024 death total. Supreme Court, Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan, PDF pp1–3 and 12–13, case context and right to walk.
sections.interpretationLimit: A share of deaths is not the risk per walking trip; victim category does not assign fault. The 2026 ruling postdates the 2024 deaths.

sections.heading: Is the pedestrian toll falling?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Table 4.4, PDF p98, 2023 and 2024 pedestrian rows; victim-category format note, PDF p96.
sections.interpretationLimit: Two reported years do not establish a long trend; pre-2019 road-user labels differ.

sections.heading: How old were the pedestrians who died?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Annexure 33, PDF p222; age and unknown-age rows checked against original scan.
sections.interpretationLimit: Age-band death counts are not risks per person or per distance walked.

sections.heading: Are older road victims more often pedestrians?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Annexure 33, PDF p222, pedestrian age rows, divided by Table 4.2, PDF p92, all road deaths in matching age bands.
sections.interpretationLimit: Within-age victim mix is not the probability of dying on a walk; no walking-exposure denominator.

sections.heading: How does the pedestrian toll differ for women and men?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Annexure 33, PDF p222, male and female pedestrian totals; narrative cross-check, PDF p96; Table 4.3, PDF p93, male and female totals of all road deaths. Within-sex shares calculated from those cells.
sections.interpretationLimit: The pedestrian share within each sex is a comparison of victim mix, not risk per walking trip or evidence of individual behaviour. Walking exposure is unavailable.

sections.heading: What vehicles were recorded in pedestrian deaths?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Table 4.5, PDF p100; source-audited road-safety artifact reused.
sections.interpretationLimit: An impacting-vehicle classification is not a legal fault verdict; Others mixes classifications.

sections.heading: Where are the largest pedestrian death totals?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Annexure 29(a), PDF p210; ten displayed state cells visually locked; all 36 state totals reconciled with Annexure 33, PDF p222.
sections.interpretationLimit: Raw state counts cannot rank risk without comparable walking exposure and reporting quality.

sections.heading: Is this only a national-highway problem?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Table 2.11, PDF p68, national-highway pedestrian deaths; Table 4.4, PDF p98, national total; remainder calculated by subtraction.
sections.interpretationLimit: All other roads is a combined remainder; road-class counts are not per-walk risks.

sections.heading: What does the right to walk require?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: Supreme Court, Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan (19 June 2026), official PDF pp5, 7, 12–13: right, local-authority duties and remedies; WHO 2023 pedestrian-safety manual, publisher page and archived HTML; MoRTH national tabulations used by this story.
sections.interpretationLimit: The judgment does not inventory footpaths or measure compliance. WHO guidance is general and does not measure the effect of an intervention in India's 2024 police data.

sections.heading: How should you read these figures?
sections.sourceRowsOrPages: MoRTH Tables 2.11, 4.2–4.5 and Annexures 29(a), 33; original PDF and source-cell audit. Supreme Court official judgment PDF pp12–13.
sections.interpretationLimit: Police returns may miss deaths; full-report SpaceBunny transcription is a reading aid, not the source of record. The 2026 judgment is a legal source, not a 2024 statistical source.
